title: Add tenant-aware metric query primitives for diagnostics + Console deep links
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Internal: adds tenant-aware metric query primitives with guardrails (allowlist, time-range caps, query budgets) for Incident Bot v2 and Console deep links.
body:
## Context
Incident Bot v2 and Console deep links need to fetch saturation + SLO-adjacent signals safely on behalf of responders without accidentally widening scope across tenants, exploding cardinality, or issuing expensive queries during an incident.

Today we have a handful of ad-hoc metric query helpers spread across console-backend and diag tooling. They differ in defaults (time windows, step, label filters) and do not consistently enforce tenant isolation.

This PR introduces a small set of primitives in `telemetry-query-service` that:
- require an explicit tenant context (or explicit opt-out for global-only metrics)
- bound query cost (time range caps, max series, max datapoints)
- allowlist which metrics/label keys can be queried from diagnostics tooling
- return structured errors suitable for bot cards ("degraded mode": show cached context + links)

## What changed (high level)
1) **TenantContext + Scoping**
- New `TenantContext` type (`tenant_id`, `deployment_mode`, `region`, `requester_principal`, `purpose`) used by all query entrypoints.
- Default enforcement: queries must include a tenant constraint unless the metric is marked `GlobalOnly` in the allowlist.

2) **Allowlisted metrics + label constraints**
- Added `MetricQueryAllowlist` with:
  - allowed metric names (e.g., `gpu.utilization`, `scheduler.queue_depth`, `kv_cache.pressure_pct`, `http.5xx_rate`)
  - allowed label keys per metric (e.g., `region`, `pool`, `model`, `route`, `tenant_id`)
  - disallowed label filters for diagnostics (prevents arbitrary regex / high-card filters)
- Console deep-link generator and incident-bot callers will only be able to query metrics present in the allowlist.

3) **Query guardrails (cost + cardinality)**
- Hard caps:
  - max lookback: 2h (configurable per purpose: `DIAGNOSTICS` vs `CONSOLE_UI`)
  - max step resolution floor: 10s
  - max series: 200 (per query)
  - max datapoints: 20k (per query)
- Soft budgets:
  - per-tenant QPS limits (token bucket keyed by `tenant_id + purpose`)
  - request coalescing key (`metric + tenant_id + time_range + filters`) to reduce burst duplication

4) **Structured errors + degraded-mode hints**
- New error type `MetricQueryError` with `code` (`FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`, `ALLOWLIST_DENY`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT`, `INVALID_FILTER`, `TOO_MANY_SERIES`), `safe_message`, and `retry_after_ms`.
- Callers can render safe user-facing messages and decide between retry, fallback links, or cached context.

5) **Tests + docs**
- Unit tests for:
  - tenant constraint enforcement
  - allowlist behavior
  - series/datapoint caps
  - budget enforcement
- Added developer docs for adding a new metric to the allowlist (including cardinality review checklist).

## Why this approach
- Keeps the enforcement close to the data access layer (telemetry-query-service), not duplicated per caller.
- Explicit tenant scoping aligns with least-privilege requirements for incident tooling and upcoming audit events (handled in PR-29133).
- Allows Console deep links to be generated consistently with the same constraints used by incident diagnostics.

## Follow-ups
- Wire these primitives into incident-bot query aggregator (tracked in ENG-5427).
- Add audit events for privileged query calls (PR-29133).
- Expand allowlist with SLO burn-rate helper metrics after alert tuning lands.

## Validation
- Local: `bazel test //telemetry-query-service/...`
- Staging: ran synthetic diag queries for 10 tenants across 3 regions; validated caps + error messages.
- Load: replayed incident-bot burst pattern from INT-3341; coalescing reduced upstream calls ~62%.

## Rollout
- Default enabled for diagnostics callers.
- Console deep link path is feature-flagged (`console.metricQueries.v2`) and will be enabled after 48h in staging.

Risk: Moderate. This touches a shared query path. Guardrails are intentionally strict; expect some initial allowlist-deny errors until callers are updated (degraded mode should handle this).
commits: telemetry-query-service: introduce TenantContext and purpose-scoped query API
telemetry-query-service: add allowlist and label filter validation
telemetry-query-service: enforce time/series/datapoint caps + structured errors
telemetry-query-service: add per-tenant budgets and request coalescing
docs/tests: add allowlist contribution guide + unit tests
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry): Can we avoid allowing arbitrary regex label filters? We had a cardinality incident last quarter. Also please confirm time range caps are enforced server-side (not just client defaults).

Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — server-side validation rejects regex filters entirely for diagnostics purpose (only exact-match allowed on allowlisted label keys). Time range caps are enforced in `guards.ts` before hitting the upstream query backend.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authz): Tenant scope enforcement looks good, but I want the API to require either (a) tenant_id or (b) an explicit `global_ok=true` with GlobalOnly metric. Otherwise callers will forget to set tenant_id and silently query global scope.
Caleb Johnson (author): Updated query route: missing tenant_id now fails with `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE` unless metric is `GlobalOnly` and caller passes `scope=global`. Added tests for both cases.
Jacob Stein (Diagnostics): For incident-bot cards, we need a stable error surface so we can render degraded-mode text consistently. Can we add `retry_after_ms` when budgets trip?
Caleb Johnson (author): Added `retry_after_ms` to `MetricQueryError` for budget + upstream 429 cases; default 30s for local budgets, passes through upstream if provided.

Chloe Martin (Console): Deep-link generator currently uses a 6h window for some dashboards. With 2h caps, links will still work but queries won’t. Can we expose caps to link builder so Console uses the same window?

Caleb Johnson (author): Added `getMaxLookback(purpose)` exported helper and updated Console deep links to default to 2h unless the destination is a dashboard link (dashboards can show longer windows without using this query API).
Nadia Rahman (Pipelines): Please ensure we’re not requiring `tenant_id` label on metrics that don’t have it yet (some GPU pool metrics are per-pool/region only).

Caleb Johnson (author): Allowlist supports `tenant_scoped=false` for region/pool metrics; in those cases we still require TenantContext but enforce scoping via `pool` + `region` constraints (and disallow querying across all pools). Documented in allowlist guide.
Logan Wright: LGTM after last push. Thanks for the guardrails and structured errors.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Approved. Please make sure callers use service identity scopes; audit events coming next PR.
Jacob Stein: Approved — error surface works for bot degraded-mode cards.
Chloe Martin: Approved — Console links updated.
